title: The Raz Book
description: A 29-chapter path through Raz 1.0
keywords: learn book tutorial chapters ownership borrowing async traits packages

title: Chapter 1: What Raz Is
description: Understand Raz's visible cost model, native execution model, and the role of Forge and LLVM.
keywords: learn book chapter Start here Compilation semantics D4000

title: Chapter 2: Create and Build a Project
description: Create a package, understand raz.toml, and learn the normal check/build/run/test workflow.
keywords: learn book chapter Start here Packages and dependencies

title: Chapter 3: Your First Program
description: Write functions, type-first parameters, semicolon-terminated statements, and documentation comments.
keywords: learn book chapter Start here Source files and declarations D1001

title: Chapter 4: Variables and Types
description: Use Raz scalar types and make numeric conversions explicit with as.
keywords: learn book chapter Start here Primitive and compound types D2009 D2289

title: Chapter 5: Arrays, Slices, References, and Pointers
description: Work with fixed arrays, borrowed slices, references, and explicit raw-pointer boundaries.
keywords: learn book chapter Start here Ownership, moves, and references D2056 D2064

title: Chapter 6: Expressions and Control Flow
description: Use operators, bool-only conditions, loops, ranges, break, continue, and return.
keywords: learn book chapter Language foundations Control flow D2007 D3006 D3007

title: Chapter 7: Structs and Methods
description: Model data with type-first fields and attach behavior through explicit impl receivers.
keywords: learn book chapter Language foundations Structs and enums

title: Chapter 8: Enums and Exhaustive Match
description: Use payload enums and exhaustive pattern matching so missing cases become compile-time errors.
keywords: learn book chapter Language foundations Pattern matching D2038

title: Chapter 9: Option, Result, and ?
description: Represent absence and recoverable failure in types and propagate failure with postfix ?.
keywords: learn book chapter Language foundations Pattern matching and recoverable errors D2047

title: Chapter 10: Ownership and Moves
description: Learn the single-owner model, explicit move, and why moved sources become unusable.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Ownership, moves, and references D2052 D2054 D2055

title: Chapter 11: Borrowing and Lifetimes
description: Use many shared or one mutable borrow with non-lexical loan analysis and safe reference escape rules.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Ownership, moves, and references D2056 D2057 D2064

title: Chapter 12: Drop and defer
description: Build deterministic cleanup with type-owned Drop and lexical LIFO defer.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Deterministic destruction D2050 D2068

title: Chapter 13: Generics
description: Write statically specialized generic functions, types, const generics, and bounded abstractions.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Generics and traits D2097

title: Chapter 14: Traits and Associated Items
description: Define reusable behavior with traits, associated items, static dispatch, and explicit dyn dispatch.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Generics and traits D2097 D2114

title: Chapter 15: Iterators and Ranges
description: Understand the Iterator and IntoIterator contracts that power for loops beyond built-in arrays.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Iteration

title: Chapter 16: Compile-Time Programming
description: Use deterministic bounded comptime execution, const functions, reflection, and layout queries.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Compile-time programming D2212 D2240

title: Chapter 17: Closures and Callable Values
description: Capture by shared borrow, mutable borrow, or move and understand callable ownership modes.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Closures and function pointers D2125

title: Chapter 18: Async, Tasks, and await
description: Use async fn, spawn, and await while preserving ownership across compiler-generated suspension frames.
keywords: learn book chapter Ownership & abstraction Async

title: Chapter 19: Modules, Packages, and Dependencies
description: Split code into modules, import namespaces, lock dependency graphs, and consume the official registry.
keywords: learn book chapter Build real software Packages and dependencies

title: Chapter 20: Standard Library
description: Navigate core, alloc, collections, and std and understand why APIs live in each layer.
keywords: learn book chapter Build real software Types and library foundations

title: Chapter 21: Concurrency and Synchronization
description: Build with threads, atomics, locks, channels, futures, tasks, timers, and cancellation.
keywords: learn book chapter Build real software Compilation semantics

title: Chapter 22: Networking and I/O
description: Use caller-controlled buffering, sockets, DNS, readiness, filesystem, and async I/O foundations.
keywords: learn book chapter Build real software Compilation semantics

title: Chapter 23: Unsafe Code and Native Interop
description: Keep extern, raw pointers, casts, and C ABI boundaries small, explicit, and auditable.
keywords: learn book chapter Build real software Unsafe code and native ABI D2289

title: Chapter 24: The Compiler Pipeline
description: Follow source through semantic analysis, typed HIR, verified MIR, Forge, LLVM, WebAssembly, and RXE.
keywords: learn book chapter Compiler & production Compilation semantics D4000

title: Chapter 25: Native Performance
description: Reason about performance across language semantics, library allocation behavior, and backend optimization.
keywords: learn book chapter Compiler & production Compilation semantics

title: Chapter 26: Diagnostics, Formatting, and Testing
description: Use stable diagnostic codes, canonical formatting, tests, and project inspection tools.
keywords: learn book chapter Compiler & production Diagnostics and implementation freedom D2008 D2009

title: Chapter 27: A Complete Small Program
description: Combine traits, generics, borrowing, enums, matching, and deterministic values in one program.
keywords: learn book chapter Compiler & production Generics and traits

title: Chapter 28: Quick Reference
description: Keep the core Raz syntax forms close at hand while writing real code.
keywords: learn book chapter Compiler & production Grammar summary

title: Chapter 29: Where to Go Next
description: Turn the tutorial into a real project: resources, modules, tests, concurrency, packages, and carefully bounded unsafe code.
keywords: learn book chapter Compiler & production Specification contents
